end.summary: Identified common non-metals and classified oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, carbon, sulphur, chlorine and iodine by state.
end.parentNote: Pari practised classifying non-metals and linking them to uses such as graphite in pencils, chlorine in water, iodised salt, nitrogen in chips packets and helium in balloons. They explained that oxygen makes up about 21% of air and that nitrogen is the larger portion. Asha also reviewed iodine as a solid and its sublimation; the lesson ended before the teach-back was passed. At home, ask Pari to make a small table of non-metals, their states and one everyday use.
